O R D E R
1. Leave granted.
2. We have heard Mr. Abhimanyu Tewari, learned counsel for the
appellant, Dr. Hemant Gupta, learned Additional Advocate General,
Haryana and Mr. Urfee Haider, learned counsel for respondent No.2,
de-facto complainant.
[
3. In this appeal, appellant has assailed legality and validity
of the order dated 01.04.2026, passed by the High Court of Punjab
and Haryana at Chandigarh (briefly the 'High Court' hereinafter)
rejecting the application for anticipatory bail of the appellant.
4. Be it stated that appellant has been named as an accused in
FIR No.779/2025, registered at Police Station Samalkha, District-
Panipat, under Sections 406, 420, 370, and 120B of the Indian Penal
1

--- Page 445 ---
Code, 1860 (for short 'IPC') and Section 24 of the Immigration Act.
5. Allegation against the appellant and the co-accused Joginder
is that they had allegedly cheated the de-facto complainant of
40,00,000/- (Rupees Fourty Lakhs only) with the assurance that₹
they would assist her in sending her son to America. The money was
allegedly taken for facilitating sending of the son of the de-facto
complainant to America. However, neither the son could go to
America nor the money refunded back to the de-facto complainant.
Rather the money has been allegedly pocketed by the accused
persons.
6. This Court by order dated 05.05.2026 had issued notice and in
the meanwhile directed that no coercive steps should be taken
against the appellant subject to the appellant cooperating with the
investigation.
7. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that pursuant to the
aforesaid order of this Court, appellant has appeared before the
Investigating Officer and has cooperated with the investigation. He
submits that appellant is a lawyer and also the brother-in-law of
the main accused Joginder. There is no allegation against the
appellant that he had actually siphoned off the money. The only
allegation against him is that he stood as guarantor when the de-
facto complainant paid the money to the accused joginder. Referring
to the statement of the appellant made before the police, he
submits that it was under duress that he had stated before the
police that he would produce accused Joginder and if he failed to
do that, he would handover a portion of his land to the victim.
8. Learned Additional Advocate General on the other hand submits
2

--- Page 446 ---
that it is a pre-planned conspiracy hatched by both the accused to
dupe the de-facto complainant of her valuable money. Appellant is
equally responsible for the crime. Referring to the statement of
the de-facto complainant made before the police, he submits that
the appellant stood as guarantor when the accused Joginder assured
to undertake various works for sending her son abroad. He had also
assured the de-facto complainant that whatever money she gave to
Joginder, he would take responsibility for the same. On a query by
the Court, he submits that Joginder Singh has now been arrested on
20.07.2026.
]
9. Learned counsel representing the de-facto complainant submits
that the allegation against the appellant cannot be segregated from
that of the other accused who is his brother-in-law. Both of them
acted in tandem to dupe the innocent de-facto complainant. Accused
Joginder has a criminal history of similar activity.
10. After hearing learned counsel for the parties and on due
consideration, we are of the view that a case for grant of
anticipatory bail is made out as against the appellant. There is no
direct allegation against the appellant that he had taken the money
on behalf of the other accused. Though the allegation is that he
stood as a guarantor for the activity of Joginder, in our view, at
the stage of consideration of bail/anticipatory bail, this factor
would not be a limiting factor to such consideration.
11. That being the position, we allow this appeal, set aside the
impugned order dated 01.04.2026 and make the order dated 05.05.2026
absolute.

IN THE SUPREME COURT OF INDIA
CIVIL APPELLATE JURISDICTION
CIVIL APPEAL NO.         OF 2026
(ARISING OUT OF SLP (CIVIL) NO. 20347 OF 2022)
FRANCISCAN SERVICE SOCIETY OF 
BANGALORE
APPELLANT(S)
VERSUS
KARNATAKA INDUSTRIAL AREA 
DEVELOPMENT BOARD & ORS.
RESPONDENT(S)
O R D E R
1. Leave granted.
2. The instant proceedings arise out of a notification dated
16.12.2006 issued under Section 28(1) of the Karnataka Industrial
Area Development Act, 1966 (“KIADA”), proposing the acquisition of
the subject land.  However, the acquisition proceedings were not
concluded within a reasonable period, as the final declaration was
not issued in due time. Aggrieved by the prolonged delay, the
appellant filed a writ petition in 2019 seeking quashing of the
acquisition proceedings.  The learned Single Judge allowed the writ
petition and held that the acquisition notification had lapsed on
account of the passage of time and inordinate delay in concluding
the proceedings. Aggrieved thereby, Respondent Nos.1 and 2, namely
Karnataka Industrial Area Development Board (KIADB) and the Special
Land Acquisition Officer, preferred an intra-court appeal, which
came to be allowed vide the impugned judgment dated 30.05.2022,
giving rise to the instant appeal.  It may be noted that, during
the pendency of the intra-court appeal, a final notification
acquiring the subject land came to be issued on 04.11.2021.
1

--- Page 470 ---
3. We have heard learned senior counsel for the parties at
considerable length.  In deference to our previous order, the KIADB
has placed on record an affidavit stating that the entire extent of
the land involved in question is lying vacant and that no orphanage
exists on the subject land, as claimed by the appellant. The
affidavit further states that the land has already been vested in
the State Government free from all encumbrances. Be that as it may,
KIADB has agreed to treat the final notification dated 04.11.2021
as the relevant date for determination of compensation payable to
the appellant.
4. The appellant, however, has reiterated the contention that an
orphanage exists on the subject land.  We are afraid that such
disputed questions of fact cannot be determined in the instant
proceedings.  In any case, with a view to ensure that the appellant
is adequately compensated, we consider it appropriate that the
compensation be determined in accordance with the Right to Fair
Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation
and Resettlement Act, 2013 (“2013 Act”).  
5. On  our  specific  query,  learned  senior  counsel  for  the
respondent State has stated that the compensation payable to the
appellant  shall  be  determined  by  treating  04.11.2021  as  the
relevant cut-off date and that such determination shall be made
strictly in accordance with the provisions of the 2013 Act.  She
further stated that the award shall be passed within a period of
two months from the date of this order.
6. In view of the aforesaid stand taken on behalf of the KIADB,
we see no ground to interfere with the impugned order.  The appeal
2

--- Page 471 ---
is, accordingly, dismissed.  It is, however, directed that the
respondents shall remain bound by the above-mentioned statement.

IN THE SUPREME COURT OF INDIA
CIVIL APPELLATE JURISDICTION
CIVIL APPEAL NO.         OF 2026
DIARY NO.30388/2026
KANAHI RAM PATEL & ORS. APPELLANT(S)
VERSUS
UNION OF INDIA & ORS. RESPONDENT(S)
O R D E R
1. Delay condoned.
2. We have heard Dr. S. Muralidhar, learned senior counsel for
the appellants and Dr. A.M. Singhvi and Mr. Atmaram Nadkarni,
learned senior counsel for respondent No.4 – Maharashtra State
Power Generation Company Limited. The relevant record has also been
perused.
3. We find that in the second round of litigation between the
parties, the Environmental Clearance (EC) granted on 11.07.2022 was
challenged before the National Green Tribunal (NGT). The NGT, vide
its judgment dated 15.01.2024, has allowed the appeal and directed
the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change to re-
examine  the  matter  from  the  stage  of  “ conducting  public
consultation afresh”.
4. In our considered opinion, the expression “ afresh” connotes
that it was obligatory upon the authorities to conduct afresh
public consultation. Since such an exercise has not been carried
out, the contrary view taken by the NGT in the impugned judgment
does not seem to be sustainable.
1

--- Page 480 ---
5. At this stage, it is stated on behalf of the appellants that
in addition to the requirement of “ afresh public consultation ”,
there were other grounds also urged before the NGT, which had not
been gone into in detail.
6. Be that as it may, since substantial compliance has already
taken place, we are satisfied that respondent No.4 is entitled to
continue with the mining activity. To that end, it is clarified
that there shall not be any impediment to respondent No.4 merely
because the requisite fresh public consultation has not been
undertaken so far. At the same time, we have no doubt that “ afresh
public consultation” ought to have been undertaken before the grant
of EC.
7. Consequently, the instant appeal is allowed in part. The
matter is remitted to the NGT, Central Zone, Bhopal to monitor that
“afresh public consultation” is carried out and that an appropriate
order is passed thereafter. If there are other issues raised by
both sides, those may also be examined on merits by the NGT.
8. It is clarified that we have not expressed any opinion on
other issues except on the issue of public consultation.
9. The  parties  are  directed  to  appear  before  the  NGT  on
03.08.2026.  We request the NGT to decide the matter expeditiously.
2

--- Page 481 ---
10. The appeal stands disposed of, accordingly.

  IN THE SUPREME COURT OF INDIA
CRIMINAL APPELLATE JURISDICTION
CRIMINAL APPEAL No.892/2026
ANIL MUNDA       APPELLANT
VERSUS
STATE OF MADHYA PRADESH     RESPONDENT
O R D E R
1. Appellant,  by  special  leave,  has  challenged  the  appellate
judgment and order of the High Court of Madhya Pradesh 1 dated
25th September, 2024, whereby his appeal2 under Section 374(2) of
the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, was dismissed.
2. In so dismissing the criminal appeal, the High Court upheld the
judgment of conviction recorded against the appellant by the trial
court under Sections 397/392 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 3 and
the order of sentence of rigorous imprisonment for 7 years plus fine
of Rs.200/- (Rupees two hundred) only.
3. We  have  heard  learned  counsel  for  the  appellant  and  the
respondent-State of Madhya Pradesh.
4. Having regard to the evidence led before the trial court, we
hold that the prosecution did prove that the appellant was guilty of
1 High Court2 Criminal Appeal No.8214 of 20223 IPC
1

--- Page 490 ---
commission of offence punishable under Section 392 of the IPC.
5. However,  insofar  as  the  finding  regarding  commission  of
offence punishable under Section 397 of the IPC is concerned, we
find that the witnesses to the seizure of the knife, allegedly used by
the appellant while robbing the complainant of Rs.2,500/- (Rupees
two thousand five hundred only), did not support the prosecution
case and turned hostile. Also, the exhibit which had been placed
before the trial court was not believed to be the knife used by the
appellant while committing the crime. 
6. In our considered opinion, the conviction under Section 397 of
the  IPC  is  doubtful and  there  is  ample  room  for extending  the
benefit of doubt to the appellant. 
7. In such view of the matter, we hold that the appellant ought
not to have been convicted under Section 397 of the IPC. He is
acquitted of such charge. 
8. We are informed that as on date, the appellant has suffered
incarceration for about four years and three months. No minimum
punishment is prescribed under Section 392 of the IPC. 
9. Having  regard  thereto  and  coupled  with  the  facts  that the
appellant had robbed the complainant of Rs.2,500/- (Rupees two
thousand five hundred) only and that he does not have criminal
history, we are of further considered opinion that sentencing the
appellant to the period of incarceration already undergone would
serve the ends of justice. Fine amount remains unaltered. Ordered
accordingly.
2

--- Page 491 ---
10. Appellant shall be set free unless wanted in any other case. 
11. Presently, the appellant is on bail; as such, he  shall stand
discharged of the bail bonds. 
  12. The criminal appeal is disposed of on the aforesaid terms.
 13. Pending application(s), if any, shall also stand disposed of.

(DIPANKAR DATTA)

        UPON hearing the counsel the Court made 
the following
                      O R D E R
1. This petition arises out of the impugned
final judgment and order dated 05.05.2026 passed
by the High Court of Gujarat at Ahmedabad in
R/Criminal Misc. Application No. 9509 of 2026,
whereby the High Court dismissed the application
filed by the Petitioner seeking regular bail in
connection  with  FIR  No.11201001250020/2025
registered at CID Crime Gandhinagar Zone Police
Station, for offences punishable under Sections
406, 409, 465, 467, 468, 471, and 120B of the
Indian Penal Code, 1860.
2. Heard  learned  counsel  appearing  for  the
Petitioner as well as learned counsel appearing
for the respondent-State of Gujarat.
3. The Petitioner has been in custody since
05.12.2025. It is pointed out by learned counsel
for the Petitioner that the investigation in the
case stands completed and the chargesheet has
SLP (Crl.) No.11052/2026 2

--- Page 503 ---
already been filed on 03.03.2026, wherein the
Petitioner has been arraigned as Accused No. 4.
The case is predominantly based on documentary
evidence which has already been collected by the
investigating agency.
4. Without expressing any opinion on the merits
of the allegations, considering the period of
incarceration undergone by the Petitioner (over
seven months), the completion of investigation,
and filing of the chargesheet, we are of the view
that a case for exercise of discretion in favour
of the Petitioner for grant of regular bail is
made out.
5. The petitioner is ordered to be released on
bail, subject to terms and conditions that the
jurisdictional court may deem fit and proper to
impose.
6. With the above directions, the Special Leave
Petition is disposed of.
SLP (Crl.) No.11052/2026 3

--- Page 504 ---
7. Pending application(s), if any, including the
application for intervention/ impleadment shall
also stand disposed of.

IN THE SUPREME COURT OF INDIA
CRIMINAL APPELLATE JURISDICTION
CRIMINAL APPEAL NO.3363 OF 2026
(@SLP(CRL.) NO.5062 OF 2026)
SITARAM BARI & ORS. APPELLANT(S)
            VERSUS
STATE OF BIHAR    RESPONDENT(S)
O R D E R
1. Heard.
2. Leave granted.
3. Appellants who are arraigned as accused in FIR No.
568/2025 for the offences punishable under Sections 316(5),
318(4) and 3(5) of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (BNS) , are
seeking for being enlarged on anticipatory bail.
4. We have heard the learned counsels appearing for the
parties. The case of the prosecution is that appellant
being a Ward Member and associated with Gram Panchayat,
Belaudi, was involved in financial irregularities while
executing ‘Nal-Jal Yojna’ Scheme. It is alleged that the
appellant has actively participated in the implementation
of the Scheme and was attributed roles relating to the
handling of financial matters, execution of the works and
certification of records. Some of the appellants alleged to
have misappropriated government funds and manipulated the
1                                                                          SLP(CRL.) NO.5062 OF 2026

--- Page 506 ---
records while one of the appellant is alleged to have
received payments through private business entity supplying
materials.
5. The learned counsel appearing for the appellants has
specifically drawn the attention of the Court to paragraph
8 of the counter affidavit whereunder the manner in which
funds were illegally rooted to the personal accounts of the
Mukhiya (Appellant No.4-Mir Imran) as well as the amount
paid to Md. Monu Sah (driver of the Mukhiya) Syed Mir
Saddam  (brother  of  the  Mukhiya)  has  been  elaborately
narrated.
6. This Court while issuing notice on 23.03.2026 had
granted interim protection in favour of the appellant(s)
subject  to  their  cooperation  with  the  investigation.
Appellant(s) have cooperated with the investigation by
appearing before the Investigating Officer (IO). As such,
there being no possibility of flight risk and stringent
conditions, if imposed by the IO, would suffice to secure
their presence.
7. Accordingly, appeal is allowed. Impugned order is set
aside.  Appellants  are  ordered  to  be  released  on
anticipatory bail on such terms and conditions as the
jurisdictional IO may deem fit to impose and also on the
condition  that  appellant  would  appear  before  the
jurisdictional trial court on all dates of hearing except
when exempted for any specific reason.
2                                                                          SLP(CRL.) NO.5062 OF 2026

--- Page 507 ---
8. Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed of.

IN THE SUPREME COURT OF INDIA
CRIMINAL APPELLATE JURISDICTION
CRIMINAL APPEAL NO.3361 OF 2026
(@SLP(CRL.) NO.3742 OF 2026)
SANJAY PODDAR ..... APPELLANT(S)
              VERSUS
STATE OF BIHAR  ..... RESPONDENT(S)
O R D E R
1. Heard.
2. Leave granted.
3. Appellant, who is arraigned as an accused in FIR No. 166 of
2025 registered for the offences punishable under Section 30(a)
of the Bihar Prohibition and Excise Act, 2022, is seeking for
being enlarged on anticipatory bail.
4. Having heard the learned counsels appearing for the parties
and on perusal of the record, it would clearly emerge therefrom
that appellant was not arraigned as an accused initially when the
FIR was registered. However, based on the statement of one Ram
Sevak, the appellant has been implicated as an accused. It is no
doubt true that there are few antecedents of similar nature
attributable  to  the  appellant.  Though  the  learned  counsel
1                                                                                         SLP(CRL.) NO.3742 OF 2026

--- Page 510 ---
appearing for the appellant would vehemently contend that even in
those cases, it is based on the statement of other accused
persons, the appellant has been arraigned as an accused, this
Court would not embark upon conducting a roving enquiry in that
regard as it is likely to prejudice the rights of either of the
parties.
5. Having regard to the fact that the appellant was not initially
arraigned as an accused when the FIR was registered and only on
the basis of the statement of co-accused, namely, Ram Sevak, who
implicated the appellant he has been roped as an accused and said
Ram Sevak, having already been enlarged on bail, we are of the
considered view that appellant is also entitled for protection at
the hands of this Court.
6. Hence, the appeal is allowed. Impugned order is set aside.
Appellant is ordered to be released on anticipatory bail by the
jurisdictional  Investigating  Officer  (10)  on  such  terms  and
conditions as he may deem fit to impose including the condition
of directing the appellant to appear before the jurisdictional
IO/PS twice a week on Monday and Saturday between 02:00 pm to
05:00 pm. IO is at liberty to impose further conditions including
the condition of directing the appellant to appear before the
trial court on all dates of hearing except when exempted for any
specific reason.
2                                                                                         SLP(CRL.) NO.3742 OF 2026

--- Page 511 ---
7. Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed of.

IN THE SUPREME COURT OF INDIA
CRIMINAL APPELLATE JURISDICTION
CRIMINAL APPEAL NO.3359 OF 2026
(@SLP(CRL.) NO.4513 OF 2026 )
NARESH KUMAR    ..... APPELLANT(S)
              VERSUS
STATE OF HARYANA ..... RESPONDENT(S)
O R D E R
1. Heard.
2. Leave granted.
3. Appellant, who has been arraigned as an accused in FIR
No.413/2024  registered  at  PS  Shivaji  Colony,  Rohtak
punishable under Sections 413(5), 103(1), 27, 25(1-B)(a) of
Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (BNS), is seeking for grant of
anticipatory bail.
4. It is the case of the appellant that on 08.07.2024,
complainant received information that his son Ravi had been
shot dead and his body was lying in a vacant plot behind
Aggarsain  Banquet  Hall.  During  investigation  police
apprehended the accused persons including Prahlad Rathi,
Krishna Rathi and Naveen from a farm house located in
Hoshiarpur.  During  interrogation  the  accused  allegedly
confessed the involvement in the crime and certain weapons
were recovered from him. The only role attributed to the
appellant is based on the statement of one Mr. Dhruv, who
1                                                                                SLP(CRL.) NO.4513 OF 2026

--- Page 514 ---
owned the farm house located at Hoshiarpur, namely, appellant
had requested Dhruv to give shelter to accused persons.
5. The case of the prosecution is that the appellant, who was
in jail, had called Mr. Dhruv and solicited his help for
hosting or sheltering the accused persons in his farm house.
Based on such disclosure statement, the appellant has been
implicated in this case.
6. As to what was the nature of communication between these
persons requires to be examined from the call detail records
between appellant and Mr. Dhruv, and this is an issue which
will have to be examined after considering the evidence that
may be tendered by the prosecution. That apart, we also
notice that said Mr.Dhruv, who is said to have harboured the
accused persons, has already been enlarged on bail. It would
suffice if appellant is to put on terms so as to allay the
apprehension  of  the  prosecution  having  regard  to  the
background of the appellant.
7. In that view of the matter we allow the appeal and
impugned order is set aside. Appellant is ordered to be
released  on  bail  on  such  terms  and  conditions  as  the
jurisdictional Investigating Officer (IO) may deem fit to
impose including the conditions: (i) that the appellant shall
appear before the IO regularly on every Thursday between
11:00 am to 05:00 pm and continue to appear on such other
dates as the IO may direct; (ii) appellant shall appear
before  the  jurisdictional  trial  court  on  all  dates  of
hearing, without fail, except when exempted for any specific
reason; and the IO would be at liberty to impose such other
conditions as he deems fit for the purpose of securing the
presence of the appellant.
2                                                                                SLP(CRL.) NO.4513 OF 2026

--- Page 515 ---
8. Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed of.

IN THE SUPREME COURT OF INDIA
CRIMINAL APPELLATE JURISDICTION
CRIMINAL APPEAL NO  . 3488   OF 2026
(@ SPECIAL LEAVE PETITION (CRIMINAL) NO. 3648/2026)
JAVED BASHIR MANSOORI      APPELLANT(S)
VERSUS
UNION OF INDIA     RESPONDENT(S)
ORDER
1. We have heard Mr. Soumya Dutta, learned counsel for
the appellant and Mr. Vikramjeet Banerjee,  learned Addl.
Solicitor General for the respondent-Union of India.
2. Leave granted.
3. In this appeal, appellant has assailed the legality
and validity of the order dated 20.01.2026 passed by the
High  Court  of  Calcutta  (briefly  the  ‘High  Court’
hereinafter), rejecting the regular bail application of
the appellant.
4. Appellant is an accused in F. No. S1(VII)-196/2025
(AIU) under Sections 20(b)(ii)(c)/29 of the Narcotics
Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act, 1985 (for short,
‘NDPS Act’).
5. Allegation against the appellant is that he was
intercepted by the Customs personnel stationed at Netaji
Subhas Chandra Bose International Airport, Kolkata and
1

--- Page 522 ---
after search, contraband of 8202 grams of Marijuana was
recovered from him. He is in custody since 21.08.2025.
6. On 11.03.2026, this Court had issued notice.
7. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that the
quantity seized from the person of the appellant is an
intermediate quantity and therefore, the rigor of Section
37 of the NDPS Act would not be attracted. He has already
undergone custody for almost a year. Further detention may
not be necessary. On a query by the Court, he submits that
appellant is a resident of Mumbai.
8. Mr. Banerjee, learned Addl. Solicitor General submits
that it is highly suspicious about the appellant using the
Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose International Airport, Kolkata,
though he is a resident of Mumbai. However, he admits that
the seized contraband is below the commercial quantity.
9. In reply, learned counsel for the appellant submits
that he came to Kolkata from Kuala Lumpur on way to
Mumbai.
10. After hearing learned counsel for the parties and on
due consideration, we are of the view that a case for
grant of bail to the appellant is made out. Accordingly,

IN THE SUPREME COURT OF INDIA
CRIMINAL ORIGINAL JURISDICTION
CRIMINAL APPEAL No.3486 OF 2026
(@ SPECIAL LEAVE PETITION (CRIMINAL) No.8457/2026
NILESH MAHARAJ @ NILESH AGNIHOTRI ..... APPELLANT(S)
              VERSUS
STATE OF MADHYA PRADESH  ..... RESPONDENT(S)
O R D E R
1. Leave granted.
2. We have heard Mr. Rahul Kaushik, learned senior counsel for
the appellant and Mr. Harmeet Singh Ruprah, standing counsel for
the State of Madhya Pradesh.
3. Appellant is aggrieved by order dated 23.02.2026, passed by
the High Court of Madhya Pradesh at Jabalpur (briefly the ‘High
Court’ hereinafter) rejecting the prayer for regular bail of the
appellant.
4. Be it stated that appellant is an accused in Crime No.461/2024
registered at Police Station Civil Lines, District- Chhatarpur for
the offences punishable under Sections 238, 127(2), 3(5), 103(1)
and 140(3) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (for short, ‘BNS’).
5. As per the allegations made in the FIR, the accused had
collectively assaulted the victim Shivam Mishra, who passed away
because of such assault. Though, appellant has not been named in
1

--- Page 542 ---
the FIR, the allegation against him as per the charge sheet is that
he was also part of the group who had assaulted the deceased and
the wallet of the deceased was recovered from him.
6. Appellant is in custody since 01.09.2024.
7. This Court  vide  order dated 13.05.2026 had issued notice
pursuant to which State has filed counter affidavit.
8. Mr. Rahul Kaushik, learned senior counsel submits that not
only  the  appellant  was  not  named  in  the  FIR,  he  has  been
subsequently roped in because of a disclosure statement of accused
Mohit Raikwar alias Mohit Don. Appellant is 22 years old and has no
previous criminal antecedents. He has completed almost 2 years of
incarceration. As to how the wallet found its way to the person of
the appellant is a matter for trial. He therefore submits that
appellant may be enlarged on bail.
9. Learned State counsel on the other hand submits that though
appellant may not have been named in the FIR, his involvement in
the offence is apparent. He himself had taken the wallet of the
deceased which was later on recovered from him. He submits that
trial has commenced and out of 41 witnesses, 11 have been examined.
Considering the seriousness of the crime, appellant may not be
enlarged on bail.
10. Submissions made by the learned counsel for the parties have
received the due consideration of the Court.
11. On a query by the Court, Mr. Harmeet Singh Ruprah, learned
State counsel submits that father of the deceased has already been
examined and cross-examined. There are no other star witnesses of
the prosecution to be examined. Having regard to the fact that
2

--- Page 543 ---
appellant is 22 years old with no criminal antecedent and has
completed about 2 years of incarceration, we are inclined to grant
bail to him.
12. Accordingly, we direct that the appellant shall be produced
before the learned Trial Court within a maximum period of 7 days
from today who shall, thereafter, enlarge the appellant on bail on
such terms and conditions as may be deemed appropriate.
13. Consequently,  impugned  order  of  the  High  Court  dated
23.02.2026 is set aside.
14. Appeal is accordingly allowed.
15. Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed of.
......................J.
(UJJAL BHUYAN)
......................J.
(ATUL S. CHANDURKAR)

          UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
1. In terms of the judgment dated 28.05.2025 in Contempt Petition
(C) Diary No. 21171/2024, the Delhi Development Authority (DDA) has
filed the Second Bi-Annual compliance report.  It is explained that
perimeter-wall construction, repair and strengthening for all 18
plantation parcels of land have now been completed, including the
last stretch at Sector-32, Rohini. Out of this, 7.86 acres Maidan
Garhi parcel has been earmarked for translocating 2,519 trees,
2

--- Page 555 ---
shrubs and saplings affected by the CAPFIMS road. It is also
pointed out that out of the sample batch of 26 plants shifted by
DDA, only 11 survived with a poor 42% survival rate, due to which
transplantation and casualty replacement were deferred to await the
monsoon period.  
2. The report further states that 1,39,264 saplings have been
planted so far across an 185-acre area constituting about 85% of
the target. The shortfall is attributed to non-availability of
specified native species, which are being procured from other
States.
3. A dedicated web portal has been operationalised to monitor the
health and survival of the saplings. A joint inspection was carried
out on 18.05.2026 at three sites, and the Expert Member found that
the  plantations  are  consistent  with  the  prescribed  species
composition and satisfactory.  
4. The report further points out that despite DRI’s failure to
deposit the allotment amount, the Dhoolsiras parcel of land was
handed over to the Forest Department on 09.06.2026, where 107 trees
have been planted, and 96 trees have been transplanted.
5. In the next status report, DDA must clarify the following
aspects:
(i) Whether the remaining 15% saplings have been planted or not?
(ii) The report based upon the web portal regarding health and
survival of the saplings be submitted.
(iii)  A separate report regarding mortality of the translocated
saplings be also submitted.
3

--- Page 556 ---
6. The process to notify all the 18 parcels of land as forest
land be also initiated.
7. Post on 21.09.2026 for the next compliance report.

Date : 27-07-2026 This matter was called on for

CORAM : HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE ARAVIND KUMAR
         HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE VIPUL M. PANCHOLI
For Petitioner(s) : Mr. Nishi Kant Singh, Adv.
                   Ms. Geetanjali Setia, Adv.

For Respondent(s) : Mr. Abhinav Bajaj, A.A.G.

--- Page 558 ---
                   Ms. Geetashi Chandna, Adv.
                   Mr. Aman Dev Sharma, Adv.
                   Mr. Gaj Singh, Adv.
                   Ms. Sabarni Som, Adv.         
   UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the 
following
                     O R D E R
1. Having heard the learned counsels appearing
for the parties and on perusal of the records, we
notice that under the impugned order, the High
Court has invoked under Section 113-B of the
Evidence Act, 1872.
2. Though it is urged by the learned counsel
appearing for the petitioner that there is no
cogent, reliable or specific evidence of cruelty
for harassment in connection with the dowry demand
“soon before the death”, that would be an issue
which will have to be examined on the basis of the
evidence that may be tendered by the prosecution
witnesses. In fact, PW-5 (father of the deceased)
in his cross-examination has admitted that no
dowry demand was made at the time of engagement or
marriage.  Even  the  evidence  of  PW-10  would
2

--- Page 559 ---
indicate that it is prima facie hearsay evidence.
In  fact,  the  letter  written  by  the  deceased
herself referred to by both the Courts which is
dated 07.02.2002 would prima facie indicate that
there  were  cordial  relationship  within  the
matrimonial family. Thus, it will have to be
examined as to whether dowry related cruelty had
occurred soon before the death as opined by the
trial judge and confirmed by the High Court and
said finding is in conformity with the evidence
that has been tendered by the prosecution.
3. For the aforesaid cumulative reasons, we are
of the considered view that petitioner is entitled
for suspension of sentence and accordingly, it has
been suspended and petitioner is ordered to be
released on bail on such terms and conditions as
the jurisdictional trial court may deem fit to
impose. This Court has also taken note of the fact
that petitioner has spent 03 years 11 months and
02 days in custody as on 27.07.2026, namely, he
has spent more than half of the sentence that has
3

--- Page 560 ---
been imposed on him.
4. Registry  to  list  this  matter  for  final
hearing on 17.11.2026. 
  (NEHA GUPTA)                      (AVGV RAMU)

IN THE SUPREME COURT OF INDIA
CIVIL APPELLATE JURISDICTION
Civil Appeal No.4602/2017
UNION OF INDIA             APPELLANT
VERSUS
N. MOHAMMED RESPONDENT
O R D E R
1. We have heard Mr. K M Nataraj, Additional Solicitor General appearing for
the appellant-Union of India and Mr. Pramod Dayal, learned counsel for the
respondent.
2. The High Court of Delhi at New Delhi 1, vide the impugned judgment and
order dated 15th April, 20152, has declined to interfere with the order of penalty
of compulsory retirement imposed on the respondent on the ground that the
advice  of  the  Union  Public  Service  Commission,  with  which  the  disciplinary
authority had concurred, was not shared with him. 
3. Such a view appears to be correct in view of the law laid down by this
Court in Union of India Vs. R. P . Singh3. 
4. Appellant-Union of  India  could  have  taken exception to the  impugned
judgment of the High Court on the ground that in terms of the law laid down by
the Constitution Bench in  L. Chandra Kumar Vs. Union of India 4,  its writ
petition  challenging  the  judgment  and  order  of  the  Central  Administrative
1 High Court
2 impugned judgment
3 (2014) 7 SCC 340
4 (1997) 3 SCC 261

--- Page 589 ---
Tribunal, New Delhi ought to have been heard by a Division Bench and not by a
Single Judge of the High Court. 
5. No such point appears to have been raised in the appeal. That the Single
Judge had no jurisdiction to hear the writ petition was not noticed by this Court
either while issuing notice or granting leave to appeal.  
6. Be that as it may, since the impugned judgment of the Single Judge of the
High Court is in accord with the law laid down in R. P . Singh (supra), we find no
reason to interfere therewith at this distance of time; hence, the civil appeal
stands dismissed.
7. Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed of.

(DIPANKAR DATTA)

Subsequently, her appointment was withdrawn

--- Page 694 ---
2
on 10.01.2024 on finding that no post for
Schedule Caste category was available and in
fact,  while  sending  requisition  to  the
recruiting body, it was never requested to
fill up any post under the Schedule Caste
category.
2. Petitioner’s  original  application
bearing O.A. No. 643/2024, was allowed by
Central  Administrative Tribunal  vide order
dated  15.10.2025  which,  has  now  been  set
aside by the High Court under the impugned
order.
3. When  this  matter  was  heard  on
19.05.2026,  learned counsel  for respondent
no.1 prayed for time to work out a solution
in the facts and circumstances of the case.
4. Now, an affidavit has been filed by
respondent  no.1  stating  the  following  in
paragraph-4 of the affidavit;
“Accordingly, the matter was discussed
in the Institute and it was decided
that the Petitioner (Ms. Shweta) can be
adjusted/ appointed against a vacant
post of HMTS (Dietary)-Kitchen Staff
under SC Category as a special case.”
5. In view of the above, the Special Leave
Petition  is  disposed  of  directing  the

--- Page 695 ---
3
respondent(s) to issue formal order allowing
the petitioner, Shweta, to join the services
on the strength of the earlier appointment
order issued i.e. on 27.12.2023.
6. Needless  to  say,  since  the  same
appointment order has to be worked on, the
petitioner,  Shweta, will  be  entitled  to
notional seniority and fixation of pay as
ordered by the Tribunal. 
7. As stated in the affidavit filed by
respondent no.1, this case is treated as a
special case and shall not be treated as a
precedent.
8. Pending application(s), if any, shall
stand disposed of.

          UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
I.A. No.105148/2026 In Civil Appeal No. 6920/2024
We have heard learned senior counsel, Shri Shyam Divan, 
for the applicant and learned counsel for the respective  
respondents and State of Maharashtra and have perused the  
interim order dated 07.05.2019 passed by this Court which has
been extended on 25.09.2019.
The prayer in the application is for enabling the  
applicant-College to make recruitment to various vacant posts.
Learned senior counsel appearing for the applicant  
submitted that the interim order granted by this Court on 
07.05.2019 and extended thereafter on 25.09.2019 ought not to
come in the way of the College making recruitment to the  
vacant posts. In this regard, he submitted that essentially 
the interim order covered 54 employees and out of them now 
only 29 to 35 persons are working. In the circumstances,  
2

--- Page 707 ---
this Court may permit the College to make recruitment to the 
vacant posts which are presently around 100 in number while 
continuing the status quo order in respect of those persons 
who are working in the College.
Learned  counsel  appearing  for  the  respondent/State  
submitted that if the necessary permissions are sought by the 
College then possibly the recruitment to the vacant posts  
could be made by the appellant. 
In the circumstances, we observe that status quo order 
dated 07.05.2019 passed by this Court which has been extended
on 25.09.2019 would not come in the way of the College  
making recruitment to the vacant posts. However, the services 
of those persons out of the original 54 persons who are  
continuing in employment, shall not in any way be affected
by the recruitment.
The  recruitment  shall  be  made  by  the  College  in  
consultation with the respondent/State.
We further clarify that the pendency of this appeal would
not come in the way of the College making the recruitment.
The application stands accordingly disposed of.

IA No.282648/2025 in Special Leave Petition (Crl.) No.15787/2025
1. This Interlocutory Application has been filed by the appellant
for enlarging him on bail pending considering of the Special Leave
Petition  (Criminal)  No.15787/2025.  It  may  be  mentioned  that
appellant was convicted by the Trial Court under Sections 120B,
396, 201, and 412 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (for short, 'IPC')
and sentenced to undergone life imprisonment.
2. Appeal filed by the appellant before the High Court was
rejected by the impugned judgment and order.
3. Aggrieved thereby, the present Special Leave Petition has been
filed. In this case notice was issued on 03.11.2025, both on the
Special Leave Petition as well as on the present Interlocutory
Application seeking bail.
4. On 30.01.2026, this Court while calling for the record,
directed listing of the case along with the connected Criminal
Appeals in the month of March, 2026 for hearing. However, no
hearing has taken place till date. In the meanwhile, we find that
as per the detention certificate issued by the competent authority
on 15.09.2025, appellant has undergone total detention of 18 years
3 months 7 days. In other words, as on today, he has undergone
incarceration for more than 19 years.
5. In the circumstances, we are of the view that a case for bail
is made out. Accordingly, we direct that pending consideration of
Special Leave Petition (Criminal) No.15787/2025, appellant shall be
enlarged on bail. For this purpose, he shall be produced before the
2

--- Page 710 ---
learned Trial Court within a maximum period of 7 days from today
and who shall, thereafter, enlarge the appellant on bail on such
terms and conditions as may be deemed appropriate.
6. Interlocutory Application No.282648/2025 is disposed of.

1. The  petitioner  seeks  enlargement  on  bail  in  FIR
No.03/2024  registered  at  Police  Station  Anti-Corruption
Bureau/Economic  Offices  Wing,  Raipur,  Chhattisgarh  for
offences punishable under Sections 420, 120-B and 384 of the
Indian Penal Code, 1860, and Sections 7, 7A and 12 of the
Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988. The petitioner was
arrested on 18.07.2025.
2. The role attributed to the petitioner is that he served
as an Accountant with the Chhattisgarh Pradesh Congress
Committee from 2000 to 2023 and thereafter became the
Personal Assistant to co-accused Ramgopal Agrawal, who was
the  Treasurer  of  the  Chhattisgarh  Pradesh  Congress
Committee. It is alleged that Ramgopal Agrawal specifically
entrusted  the  petitioner  with  the  task  of  collecting
extortion money and introduced him to co-accused Suryakant
Tiwari for this purpose. The illegal coal levy allegedly
collected by the associates of Suryakant Tiwari was then,
purportedly on the instructions of the petitioner, handed
over to him at Congress Bhawan, Raipur.
3. On  the  previous  date  of  hearing,  the  matter  was
adjourned to enable the Investigating Agency to confront the
petitioner with the version of Ramgopal Agrawal, who had,
meanwhile,  been  arrested.  Learned  State  counsel  fairly
states that the said part of the investigation is over.
2

--- Page 713 ---
4. In view of the aforesaid, and having regard to the fact
that the petitioner’s co-accused have already been released
on bail and that the conclusion of trial will take a
reasonable time, as there are 234 witnesses cited by the
prosecution  and  the  case  involves  21  accused  persons,
however, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the
case, we are satisfied that the petitioner can be released
on bail. Ordered accordingly.
5. The petitioner is directed to be released on bail
subject to his furnishing bail bonds to the satisfaction of
the Trial Court and subject to all other such terms and
conditions  which  have  been  imposed  on  his  co-accused,
namely, Narayan Sahu, in SLP(Crl.) No.9231/2026.
6. The Special Leave Petition is, accordingly, disposed
of.
7. All pending applications, if any, also stand disposed
of.

By  order  dated  18.05.2026,  this  Special  Leave
Petition was disposed of directing the respondent in the
Special Leave Petition to enable the petitioner herein to
meet the minor daughter on every Sunday starting from
06.06.2026 at any Mall in Delhi during 05:00 PM to 08:00
PM, which is to be mutually decided prior to the meeting.
For ease of reference, the said order is extracted as
1

--- Page 739 ---
under:
“We  have  heard  learned  counsel  for  the
petitioner and learned counsel for the respondent.
We  direct  the  respondent  to  enable  the
petitioner herein to meet the minor daughter on
every Sunday starting from 06.06.2026 at any Mall
in Delhi between 05:00 PM to 08:00 PM, which is to
be mutually decided prior to the meeting.
It  is  needless  to  observe  that  the
respondent shall enable the petitioner to fulfill
these visitation rights in both letter and spirit,
which implies that the respondent shall not cause
any disturbance from the aforesaid hours.
The  respondent-mother  is  at  liberty  to
accompany the petitioner as well as the child.
The petitioner is also at liberty to enable
his mother to meet the child.
With the aforesaid observations, we dispose
of this Special Leave Petition by reserving liberty
to the parties to seek all other reliefs before the
appropriate forum.
Pending application(s), if any, shall stand
disposed of.” 
Application has now been filed by the respondent-
mother of the minor child for appropriate orders as to
whether the aforesaid order dated 18.05.2026 is restricted
to the period of Summer Vacation or whether it has to be
extended beyond the said period. This application has been
made in response to the request made by the petitioner
herein  for  continuing  the  said  order  even  after  the
conclusion of the Summer Vacation. 
We have heard learned counsel for the respondent-
mother of the minor daughter and learned counsel for the
petitioner in the presence of the respective parties.
We dispose of this Application by observing that the
petitioner in the Special Leave Petition shall be entitled
to meet the minor daughter on every second and fourth
2

--- Page 740 ---
Saturdays of the month starting from 08.08.2026 at any
Mall in Delhi between 05:00 PM to 08:00 PM, which is to be
mutually decided prior to the meeting.
The rest of the order of this Court dated 18.05.2026
shall be read as part and parcel of this order.
It is needless to observe that this order shall be
subject to the final order to be passed by the Family
Court in the Custody Petition which has been filed by the
petitioner-father.
It is stated at the bar that application for interim
maintenance has been filed by the respondent-wife, both
for her as well as for the minor daughter, which is
pending consideration before the concerned Family Court.
The  said  application  shall  be  decided  as
expeditiously as possible and preferably within a period
of two months from 19.08.2026.
Miscellaneous  Application  is  disposed  of  in  the
above terms.
Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed
of.

O R D E R
1. This Miscellaneous Application has been filed by Adani Power
Limited, the successful resolution applicant of Vidarbha Industries
Power Limited, seeking clarification of this Court’s order dated
18.05.2026 in Civil Appeal No. 7974 of 2026.
2. By the said order, while construing paragraph 12 of the NCLT’s
order dated 18.06.2025 approving the Resolution Plan, this Court
clarified that the sum of Rs.1 crore earmarked for operational
creditors, in respect of which the employees were to have the first
preferential claim, was payable in addition to the amounts due
towards the employees’ provident fund and gratuity.
3. The  clarification  now  sought  is  whether  the  amount  of
Rs.65,17,076/-, comprising provident fund, gratuity and interest,
is to be distributed  pro rata  amongst all eligible operational
creditors or exclusively amongst the eligible employees.
4. It is thus clarified that the amount of Rs.65,17,076/- shall
be disbursed amongst the eligible employees only.

of, accordingly, with pending application(s), if any.

         HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE ARUN PALLI
For Petitioner(s) : 
                   Mr. Shubhranshu Padhi, AOR
                   Mr. Jay Nirupam, Adv.

For Respondent(s) :

                   Mr. Vikash Kumar, Adv.
                   Mr. Tarun Bhati, Adv.
                   Ms. Sadaf Husain, Adv.
                   Mr. Tejasv Gupta, Adv.
                                    
          UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
1. Heard  Mr.  Shubhranshu  Padhi,  learned  counsel
appearing  for  the  petitioner  and  Ms.  Bharti  Tyagi,
learned counsel appearing for the respondent-State.
1

--- Page 785 ---
2. Having heard the learned counsel for the parties
and perused the records, we are of the opinion that in
the  present  case,  it  could  not  be  said  that  the
prosecution was substantially responsible for delaying
the trial.  It is not disputed that between 2010-2011 and
21st December, 2022 when the order of framing charges was
passed, the proceedings dragged on due to applications
moved by the accused.
3. In the peculiar facts and circumstances, we are of
the opinion that this is not a case which could be
quashed on the ground of denial of speedy trial under
Article 21 of the Constitution of India.  The Special
Leave Petition is, accordingly, dismissed.
4. We, however, considering the fact that the trial is
of the year 2002, direct the Trial Court to conclude the
proceedings, as expeditiously as possible, in any event,
not later than one year from today.
5. Pending  application,  if  any,  shall  also  stand
disposed of.

PRESIDENT, DEVASTHAN STHANIK SALLAGAR SAMITEE       Respondent(s)
IA No. 211758/2026 - EXEMPTION FROM FILING C/C OF THE IMPUGNED 
JUDGMENT
IA No. 211759/2026 - EXEMPTION FROM FILING O.T. 
Date : 28-07-2026 This matter was called on for hearing today.
CORAM : HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE ARAVIND KUMAR
         HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE VIPUL M. PANCHOLI
For Petitioner(s) : Mr. Anand Dilip Landge, AOR
                   Mr. Chetan Patil, Adv.
                                      
For Respondent(s) : Mr. Srikrishna Ganbavale, Adv.
                   Mr. Shantanu M. Adkar, Adv.
                   Mr. M. Y. Deshmukh, AOR                        
          UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
1. Having heard the learned counsels appearing for the parties,
we notice that courts-below, namely, the trial court and the
appellate court on appreciation of facts have negatived the prayer
of  temporary  injunction  by  taking  note  of  three  ingredients
necessary for grant of temporary injunction, namely, prima facie
case, balance of convenience and irreparable loss and injury being
absent or in other words, the application for temporary injunction
has been rejected though initially order of status quo had been
granted.  Notwithstanding,  the  said  order  of  dismissal,
surprisingly, the courts-below still extended its olive branch by
granting the order of status quo. However, we do not propose to
express any opinion in this regard and we leave at it.
2. Be that as it may, the petitioners, namely, the unsuccessful
1

--- Page 899 ---
plaintiffs being aggrieved by the abovesaid order of temporary
injunction being refused had pursued their grievance by filing an
appeal, weherein order of  status quo  was initially granted on
17.02.2026 and ultimately the appeal came to be dismissed on
28.04.2026. However, by a separate order of even date (Annexure P-
8), the appellate court extended the order of status quo by four
(4) weeks. Being aggrieved by the dismissal of the appeal by
appellate court order, a Writ Petition came to be filed by the
unsuccessful plaintiffs before the High Court and the matter is
still pending before the High court and for non-continuation of
status  quo  which  was  earlier  granted  by  the  High  Court  on
08.05.2026, the petitioners (plaintiffs) are before this court
seeking for the said order being extended till disposal of the Writ
Petition.
3. As noticed hereinabove, the High Court having arrived at a
conclusion that  prima facie  case not being in favour of the
plaintiff has refused to grant the temporary injunction and / or
has refused to extend the order of status quo. Hence, we are not
inclined to grant the said prayer at this stage. Even otherwise,
the petition under Article 227 of the Constitution of India
assailing the order of the first appellate court is still pending
before the High Court and we would only request the High Court to
dispose of the Writ Petition expeditiously.
4. With the aforesaid observations, Special Leave Petition stands
disposed of. 
5. Pending application(s), if any, shall also stand disposed of.
  (NEHA GUPTA)                                   (AVGV RAMU)
COURT MASTER (SH)                             COURT MASTER (NSH)

For Respondent(s) : 
          UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
1. Delay condoned.
2. The submission of the learned counsel for the
petitioner is that the Corporation had the right to
compulsorily retire its employee after he has attained
the age of 50 years or on the concerned date has
completed 25 years of service, whichever is earlier.
3. It is submitted that in paragraph 4 of the writ
petition, the writ petitioner has himself admitted that
he has rendered almost 26 years of service.  In ground
‘c’ of the appeal preferred before the Division Bench
of the High Court a specific plea was raised by the
petitioner that the writ petitioner had completed 25
years of service and, therefore, the finding to the
contrary is incorrect.  It has also been urged that the
Division Bench as well as the Single Judge of the High
Court  committed  error  in  equating  service  with
qualifying service because qualifying service is for
the purpose of eligibility to pension.
4. Issue notice, returnable in eight weeks.
5. In the meantime, the effect and operation of the
impugned order shall remain stayed.

1

--- Page 1321 ---
2. In our considered view, the High Court ought not to have passed
the order when the petitioner(s) has filed an appeal before the
District Judge. Considering the same, if we dispose of the present
Special Leave Petitions as having become infructuous, that would
not be correct.
3. In such view of the matter, the impugned order is set aside and
the appeal bearing CMA No.23/2023 is restored on the original file
of the District Judge and we direct the District Judge to decide
the same on merits within a period of nine months from the date of
receipt of a copy of this order.
4. Since the petitioner is dispossessed and the order has been
challenged before us, the appellate court shall consider the appeal
in  accordance  with  law  without  going  into  the  issue  of
dispossession in pursuance to the order passed by the High Court.
5. The Special Leave Petitions stand disposed of in the aforesaid
terms.
6. Pending application(s), if any, shall also stand disposed of.

parties for release of suitor’s fund amount.
2. Considering the above referred facts, this Court is of the
opinion that this Court can exercise its discretion under Rule 7,
Order XXIV of the Supreme Court Rules, 2013 by allowing the
disbursement of the suitor’s fund amount of Rs. 50,000/- (Rupees
fifty thousand) in favour of the Armed Forces Battle Casualties
Welfare Fund (AFBCWF).
